newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel braces for PLO anti-settlement protest.
newsitem.headline: Israel braces for PLO anti-settlement protest.

text.p: Israeli security forces deployed throughout Arab East Jerusalem on Friday ahead of a Palestinian demonstration against Israel's plans to build a new Jewish settlement in that side of the holy city.
"We have information that there is tension in the air," newly-appointed Jerusalem police chief Yair Yitzhaki told Israel Radio.

He characterised a Palestinian march set to go from Beit Sahur village south of Jerusalem to the site designated for the new settlement as a "demonstration of force". Palestinians have called for a peaceful protest.

"There are calls from all directions not to disturb the peace and not to confront the security forces. We are deployed in large numbers for the possibility of such a confrontation...I very much hope there will not be one," he said.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government enraged Palestinians on February 26 when it approved a plan to build 6,500 new homes for Jews at Jabal Abu Ghneim hill in East Jerusalem, known as Har Homa to Israel.
Yitzhaki said 2,500 police were deployed at Har Homa and in Jerusalem's walled Old City, site of al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine, where weekly Moslem Friday prayers were to be held.
Demonstrators plan to hold Moslem prayers at the Har Homa site.
Palestinian Authority minister Elias Freij, the mayor of Bethlehem which is just south of Har Homa, called on Netanyahu to stop settlement and pursue peace.
"I tell Mr Netanyahu Jews and Palestinians are destined by God to live in this country together and forever," Freij said.
"So which is best: to live in peace as good neighbours or to remain as enemies quarrelling, fighting and shouting and suffering and screaming?"
Palestinians on Friday slammed Israel's unilateral decision early in the morning on a further troop withdrawal in the West Bank as insufficient and a violation of their peace accords.
After a seven-hour overnight debate Israel's cabinet voted 10-7 to back a proposal by Netanyahu to hand over another nine percent of the West Bank to the Palestinians, said a government spokeswoman.
Two percent is land exclusively under Israeli control; seven percent is land that had been patrolled by both Israel and the PLO.
In a U.S.-brokered deal by which Israel handed over most of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian rule in January, Israel agreed to carry out three further withdrawals.
Palestinians say they had understood Israel would withdraw from 90 percent of the occupied land but the Jewish state insists the scope of the pullbacks are solely up to it.
Final borders are to be decided in permanent status talks scheduled to begin this month where Jerusalem's status is also to be negotiated.

Israel captured Arab East Jerusaelm in the 1967 Middle East war and, in a move not recognised by the international community, annexed it shortly afterward. Palestinians want East Jerusalem as capital of a future state.
